question: Should OpenClaw adopt this repository-wide QA policy: one globally unique exact `<surface-id>.<feature-id>` ID per taxonomy feature, catalog-owned semantic attribution, and an evidence-bounded 11-category `smoke-ci` profile?
rationale: The patch is internally validated, but selecting the permanent semantics of maturity accounting and CI smoke-profile scope is a maintainer QA-policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Adopt the strict contract
options.body: Merge after refreshing the merge result and required checks, accepting the catalog as the sole semantic coverage owner and the narrower evidence-bounded smoke profile.

options.title: Keep broader smoke eligibility
options.body: Request a focused follow-up that preserves the exact-ID contract but restores any broader `smoke-ci` categories maintainers intentionally want eligible beyond the fixed plan.

options.title: Pause for QA policy review
options.body: Hold this large migration until QA owners document the intended relationship between maturity profiles, fixed smoke plans, and producer evidence.

recommendation.title: Adopt the strict contract
recommendation.body: Merge after refreshing the merge result and required checks, accepting the catalog as the sole semantic coverage owner and the narrower evidence-bounded smoke profile.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current contributor with the most direct evidence for the proposed QA coverage model; additional QA-owner review is still appropriate.
